newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ansett set to sell Diners Australia stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ansett set to sell Diners Australia stake - paper.

text.p: Regional airline Ansett Australia is about to sell its 68.2 percent stake in Diners Club's Australian franchise for up to A$43 million to a local or overseas bank, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper said on Thursday.

"Ansett has already called for expressions of interest for its stake in Diners Club and it is believed that the cut-off date has expired, with about six parties showing their hand," the newspaper said.
Those parties included Westpac Banking Corp, National Australia Bank Ltd, ANZ Banking Group Ltd, Citibank and GE Capital Corp, the Herald said.
Ansett is jointly owned by News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand Ltd.
Ansett, which is struggling to regain profitability, has said it would sell non-core assets like tourist resorts and the Diners Club stake.
The newspaper said Diners Club would keep its frequent flier programme with Ansett after the stake was sold.
The remaining interest in Diners Club is held by Diners Club International, with 22.7 percent, and by Diners Club Japan, with 9.1 percent.
